subject: Confusion regarding multisession models and single session models

messages.author: 625b44a5a4f8beeb
messages.subject: Confusion regarding multisession models and single session models
parts:
Hi!
I am estimating the densities of tigers and leopards in Central India using MLSECR. I have used both single session and multiple session SECR models to estimate the densities. The estimates are coming different in the two cases (although the confidence intervals are overlapping). I am little confused about this. Can you please tell me why this might be the case?

Additionally the models which are being selected in single session and multiple session are different. In case of tigers, the best model for the all sessions using single session models were (D~1,g0~h2,sigma~1). For tigers, the best model in multiple session SECR was (D~session,g0~h2+session,sigma~h2+session). In case of leopards, the best models were (D~1,g0~h2,s~1) and (D~1,g0~1,s~h2) in session 1 and both sessions 2 & 3 respectively. When multiple session models were run for the same dataset, the best model as per AIC value as (D~session,g0~h2+session,sigma~h2+session). I am a little confused about the reason behind this.

I have also used sex of the identified individuals as a covariate  for hybrid mixture models: secr.fit(TCH, mask=pmask,binomN =1,model = list(D~1,g0~1,sigma~1), hcov='sex', verify=F). Can this individual covariate used to estimate sex-specific density?

Thanks in advance,
Anindita

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Confusion regarding multisession models and single session models
parts:
Hi Anindita
You should expect different models (single session vs multi-session) to give different estimates, but the difference will be large only if the data are sparse (or session differences large and unmodelled).
I can't see quite what your issue is with model selection (your second paragraph).
The hybrid mixture models estimate a parameter 'pmix' that is the sex ratio - not quite sex-specific density, but perhaps OK?
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Confusion regarding multisession models and single session models
parts:
OK - if not due to sparse data there must be something odd (and probably wrong) about your implementation. The need for multisession models is usually obvious from the structure of the data (e.g. separate blocks of sampling in time or space), although sometimes 'sessions' can be used for subgroups within one population (e.g. sexes). We just don't know enough about what you are doing. Feel free to try again with more detail and a specific question.
Murray
